review_notes: It's unresolved whether the current dragon is the same dragon from Sir Brandon's myth or a new one; the GM left this ambiguous, so no required question asserts either way.
Squints collecting a sample of the dead ooze is a minor keepsake detail with unclear future relevance, so it is offered as optional rather than required.
The goblins' agreement to escort the party through the barrow is a minor logistical detail that mainly restates their cooperative stance already established elsewhere, so it is offered as optional.
Snurk's rebuke of Squints largely restates the hierarchy-free ideology already voiced by Grimble, so it is offered as optional rather than a separate required fact.
The statue labeled Wisdom is only presumed to be Brandon in the source material; this uncertainty is preserved in the corresponding question rather than treated as confirmed identity.
The silver dagger at the bottom of the pool was never explicitly retrieved; Brother Dirk brought up the skull instead, leaving the dagger's fate unresolved.
The slime's claim about a large, still-moving creature that killed the goblins is preserved as an attributed claim rather than an established fact, since no independent narration confirms it.
The ultimate disposition of the jeweled chalice (whether it went to the church or elsewhere) is left unresolved after Trout's deflection; no required question asserts a final outcome for it.
The detail that Phidipaldi found only dust inside the urns was omitted as a negative observation with no stated consequence.
